ignore.reason: NewReader plus Next already performs one-shot decoding with source and diagnostic output. Reduced one-shot wrappers add no distinct Go operation.

Reader keeps its window, consumed prefix, absolute base and finality in Go; SetInput, Offset and AtEnd expose these operations without a persistent native sequential cursor. TreeReader delegates its structural window changes to Core.
TreeReader.Next and NextEvent use diagnostic variants and project their source metadata; reduced-output wrappers add no public operation.

Reader.Visit and TreeReader.Visit are Go callback adapters over canonical diagnostic pulls. They preserve stop/resume, input pauses and borrowed views while returning application errors unchanged and guarding callback reentrancy; no cgo callback trampoline is needed.

Writer and TreeWriter retain copied tags and staged values in Go-owned frames; Finish checks those frames. TreeWriter enforces depth/count budgets and delegates encoding to diagnostic Writer/Tree Writer operations. Caller-owned native tag/scratch storage is intentionally replaced by Go allocation, not exposed as an allocation-free guarantee.

WriteEvent checks balanced kind/depth/skipped rules in Go and dispatches to the existing diagnostic Begin/Write/End operations. EncodeTree/EncodeEvents and MeasureTree/MeasureEvents stage through that same writer, including content-dependent encoding. Native callback/workspace variants duplicate these operations with different storage ownership.
Writer.Measure accepts actual content and uses tlv_element_encoded_size_diag; length-only or no-diagnostic measurement offers no additional wire capability.

Writer.Write/WriteElement stage and commit through tlv_write_element_diag. Cursor, copy-element and tag/value variants re-encode the same logical input; Go owns the output position and transactional publication.
Writer.Remaining reports fixed root capacity directly from its Go slice, with an explicit distinction for growable output; Preserve uses the diagnostic native variant.
Go byte slices, copy, equality and checked native-size conversions represent these storage primitives; wire decoding and encoding still delegate to Core.
Reader.Next uses tlv_reader_next_source_diag to preserve both source spans and diagnostics; these reduced-output wrappers add no separate public operation.
Writer uses tlv_write_element_diag and tlv_tree_writer_begin_diag/end_diag; the no-diagnostic wrappers add no separate public operation.

Callbacks selected by tlv_fixed_format_init for NewFixed; Core invokes them through the format descriptor. The referenced tlv_binary_decode identity check remains counted as a reference, not a separate public operation.

Callbacks installed by the inline tlv_number_codec, tlv_text_codec and tlv_digits_codec constructors used by NumberCodec, TextCodec and DigitsCodec; Go invokes tlv_codec_decode/encode on those descriptors.

Core constructors install these callbacks for NewComposed, NewEscaped and NewVariable. Reader/Writer, Document and Query invoke the resulting descriptors; direct callback APIs would duplicate these operations without Core's wrapper checks.

NewComposed with fixed identifier/length encodings and TagOnly exposes the same generic tagged binary operation through the broader tagged-fields constructor; a second public constructor adds no functionality.
Writer.Measure and WriteElement already expose canonical format measurement and encoding through richer diagnostic wrappers; Format.Preserve separately exposes exact source preservation.
